CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAJESH RAI K  ORAL ORDER

This petition is filed under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023 in Criminal Misc.No.864/2025, pending on the file of IV Additional District and Sessions Judge, Vijayapura, primarily on the ground of health of the petitioner seeking Regular Bail.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge, Vijayapura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for the petitioner has contended that the petitioner is suffering from Vitreous Hemorrhage with tractional bands (left eye) and there is a serious threat of sudden vision loss.

3. On perusal of the records, this Court vide order dated 03.11.2025 passed the order as under:
NC: 2026:KHC-K:21 HC-KAR "1.

The petitioner, despite having suffered an order of cancellation of bail by the Hon'ble Apex Court, has once again approached this Court seeking regular bail on the ground that he requires advanced medical treatment, as evidenced by the medical certificate issued by the attending doctor, found at page 40 of the records.

2. Learned counsel appearing for the complainant does seriously dispute the petitioner's health condition, it is submitted in the statement of objections that the certificate relied upon by the petitioner is dated 20.05.2025.
In the absence of an opinion from a duly constituted Medical Board, it is contended that the petitioner is attempting to secure bail on medical grounds without sufficient or credible medical Sri.

Shankargouda @ Shankarling vs The State Of Karnataka on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68329615/
2 substantiation.

entities.text: Shankargouda @ Shankarling vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. The learned High Court Government Pleader, while opposing the petition, submits that unless the petitioner produces cogent and credible medical evidence to demonstrate a change in circumstances, the earlier order of the Hon'ble Apex Court continues to operate, and considering the persisting threat to the victim's family, the petitioner is not entitled to be enlarged on bail.

4. Having heard the rival submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned HCGP for the State, and the learned counsel for respondent No.2/complainant, this Court is of the considered view that the plea of bail on medical grounds requires due consideration.

However, in view of the earlier rejection of bail by the Hon'ble Apex Court, the petitioner must substantiate that his health NC: 2026:KHC-K:21 HC-KAR condition necessitates specialized treatment which cannot be adequately provided in custody.

5. Since the certificate relied upon by the petitioner is dated 20.05.2025, this Court deems it appropriate to direct that the petitioner be referred to the Medical Board of the District Government Hospital, Vijayapura.

The Medical Board shall thereafter furnish its report to this Court through the Superintendent of Jail on or before the next date of hearing.
Re - list this matter on consideration.

4. In compliance of the said order, the jail authorities have taken the petitioner for Medical Board of the District Government Hospital, Vijayapura.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
The District Surgeon, along with the concerned ophthalmologist examined the petitioner and submitted a certificate as under:
"We the members of Medical Board district Hospital Vijayapur.

Examined Mr.
Shankaraling s/o Appasaheb Biradar Age:54Y/F.

Address:
Darga Jail, Vijayapur Tq: Dist: Vijayapur.
His OPD No.20250244310 on 17/11/2025 at District NC: 2026:
KHC-K:21 HC-KAR Hospital Vijayapur.

He was diagnosed as Vitreous hemorrhage with tractional band (left eye).
Referred to higher centre for further evaluation and management as vitreoretina facility not available at our district hospital, Vijayapur."

5. The certificate reveals that the petitioner/patient was referred to higher center for further evaluation and management as vetreotina facility is not available at the District Hospital,
Vijayapura.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that those facilities are available at Anugraha Hospital,
Vijayapura.

7. Since the medical certificate reveals that the petitioner is suffering from vitreous hemorrhage with tractional band (left eye), it is appropriate to direct the Jail Authorities of District Prison, Vijayapura to take the petitioner to Anugraha Hospital at Vijayapura for higher treatment, as observed in the Medical Board Certificate dated 17.11.2025.

It is needless to mention that the Jail NC:
2026:KHC-K:21 HC-KAR Authorities shall take all the precautions by providing necessary guards to escort the petitioner to the said hospital.

If the doctor of the said hospital advise to admit the petitioner in the said hospital, the Jail Authorities shall also escort and guard the petitioner in the hospital throughout his stay in the hospital.
The Jail Authorities shall permit the family members of the petitioner to attend the patient and to contact the doctors.
After such treatment, the petitioner shall be sent back to the Central Prison and a detailed report shall be placed before the Trial Court.
With these observations, the petition stands disposed of.
